content.text:
This is the as-found single-line diagram of a building's 480 V switchgear. Utility 2 is out of service, so standby generator G1 is running and carries every load it is connected to through closed breakers. Then main breaker 52-M1 trips. The operator restores power with this procedure: (1) find the loads that were running before the trip and lost power; (2) tie breaker 52-T (now open) will be closed, which re-energizes only what can then be reached from G1 through closed breakers; (3) G1's rating is printed next to it on the drawing; if G1's total load after closing 52-T would exceed that rating, the operator first opens the load breakers of loads that 52-T would restore, one at a time, largest kW first, until the total is at or below the rating; (4) the operator closes 52-T. No other breaker changes position. A load behind an open breaker was not running before the trip. What is the total kW of the loads that were running before the trip and are not running at the end (loads shed in step 3 plus loads 52-T cannot reach)? Answer with an integer number of kW.

Think step by step. Then end your reply with one final line in exactly this form:
FINAL ANSWER: <your answer>

message.content:
## Answer: 421 kW

**1. Loads running before the trip.** Utility 1 feeds Bus 1 through closed 52-M1. Utility 2 is out, so 52-M2 is open. G1 feeds Bus E through closed 52-G1, and Bus 2 is tied to Bus E through closed 52-ET. Bus 2 is therefore energized from G1. PNL-2B (BUS 2B) is fed from both Bus 1 (CB-04) and Bus 2 (CB-06).

**2. Loads lost when 52-M1 trips.** Only Bus 1 and the loads fed solely from it lose power:
- RP-3, via CB-01: 57 kW
- MCC-1B through CB-03: LP-2 46 kW, EF-4 22 kW, LAB-2 101 kW
- UPS-1, via CB-05 and CB-14: 195 kW

EL-1 (CB-15 open) was not running. PNL-2B, KP-1, and the Bus E loads stay energized from G1 through 52-ET.

Lost total: 57 + 46 + 22 + 101 + 195 = 421 kW.

**3. Reach of 52-T.** Closing 52-T connects dead Bus 1 to G1-energized Bus 2. All five lost loads are reachable through closed breakers, so 52-T restores all of them. None are unreachable.

**4. Load check in step 3.** Loads already on G1 after the trip are BP-1 29, CT-1 90, CH-1 345, KP-1 76, CRAH-4 35, CH-2 305 and FP-1 85, totaling 965 kW. Adding the 421 kW restored gives 1386 kW against a 575 kW rating. Shedding the restored loads in descending order (UPS-1 195, LAB-2 101, RP-3 57, LP-2 46, EF-4 22) only brings the total down to 965 kW, which is still above 575 kW. Every restored load is therefore shed.

**5. Result.** No lost load comes back, so the loads not running at the end are the full 421 kW (all shed in step 3, none unreachable).

FINAL ANSWER: 421

Now I'm checking which loads on Bus 1 lose power when 52-M1 trips, since the tie to Bus 2 is open and nothing else feeds it. The MCC-1B loads, UPS-1, and RP-3 all drop out. PNL-2B stays energized from G1 through Bus 2 and CB-06, so BP-1, CT-1, CH-1, and KP-1 keep running.

Next I'm adding up the loads that drop when 52-M1 trips, which comes to 421 kW. Then I'm looking at closing 52-T to reconnect Bus 1 to the energized Bus 2, and checking how much of Bus 1's load G1 could pick up through the MCC-1B feeders.

I'm totaling the loads that stay energized from G1 once 52-T closes: the PNL-2B feeds, KP-1, and the Bus E loads, which comes to 965 kW against G1's 575 kW rating.

I'm adding up the loads that stay on G1 after the trip, which is 965 kW, and comparing that against the generator's 575 kW rating. I'm also noting that the PNL-2B feed through CB-04 is on the dead side of the bus now.

I'm working out how the load shifts once 52-T closes: restoring Bus 1 would push G1 to about 1386 kW against its 575 kW rating, so I need to shed loads. The plan is to open breakers on the loads 52-T would bring back, starting with the largest, UPS-1 at 195 kW, until the total fits under the rating.

Shedding only the restored loads still leaves the total well above 575 kW, since the 965 kW already on G1 comes from loads that were running before the trip. Before I decide what to shed, I want to recheck whether those loads really all sit on G1.

I'm confirming that Bus 2 and Bus E are both fed from G1 through the closed 52-ET tie, so the loads on them, about 965 kW in total, already exceed G1's 575 kW rating before any shedding.

I'm noticing that the load total stays near 965 kW even before any shedding, which is well above G1's 575 kW rating, so shedding only the restored loads can't bring it down far enough. I'm wondering whether the question means the total only after closing 52-T, or whether loads that were running before the trip are also being shed at the end.

I'm working through whether shedding every restored load is enough, since then the lost loads would all stay off, so the total left dark would be 421 kW.

I'm checking whether 52-T reaches every lost load, and tracing the Bus 1 breakers to see if any of them are cut off from it.

I'm checking that the Bus 1 loads stay reachable after 52-T closes, and that the only breakers still open are CB-02, CB-09, and CB-15. The restored load of 421 kW plus the 965 kW already on G1 gives 1386 kW against the 575 kW rating, so the shedding rule can't bring the total down to the rating.

Shedding only the restored loads still leaves G1 well over its 575 kW rating, since the 965 kW already on it was running before the trip. I'm weighing whether the shedding step can ever reach the rating, and if it can't, that all the restored loads would end up off and the total left dark would be 421 kW.

I'm weighing whether shedding in order from largest to smallest could ever bring the total down to 575 kW, and it can't, since the 965 kW already on G1 leaves the restored loads with nothing to cut below the rating. So every restored load ends up shed, leaving 421 kW off.

I'm settling on the answer now: since shedding only the restored loads can't bring G1 down to its rating, every restored load has to go, which leaves 421 kW dark. I want to be sure the shedding wouldn't stop short of that before I commit.

I'm checking whether shedding only some of the restored loads could bring the total down, and the 965 kW already on G1 means it can't reach 575 kW either way. So I'm settling on the 421 kW figure, and I'll double-check the pre-trip loads on PNL-2B before finalizing.
